Series::silu¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::silu() const -> Series
Series& Series::silu_()
Series& Series::silu_() const

What It Does¶

silu() applies the Sigmoid Linear Unit (also called swish) elementwise:

silu(x) = x * sigmoid(x)

Like gelu() it is a smooth, self-gating activation: each input is scaled by its own sigmoid(), so large positive x passes through nearly unchanged, x = 0 maps to 0, and negative x is softly suppressed.

It is not monotonic. For x slightly negative the product x * sigmoid(x) dips to a minimum of about -0.278 near x = -1.278 before rising back toward 0. That small non-monotonic region is a deliberate feature — it lets the activation represent a mild negative response rather than a hard cutoff.

silu() needs a floating-point input.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& The activated values, same shape and floating-point dtype as the input. silu_() overwrites the current storage.

Gradient¶

silu() is differentiable. With s = sigmoid(x):

d/dx silu(x) = s + x * s * (1 - s) = s * (1 + x * (1 - s))

It equals 0.5 at x = 0, goes slightly negative in the same region where the forward value dips, and tends to 1 for large positive x and 0 for large negative x.

In-Place Form¶

silu_() is the in-place sibling of silu(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — silu_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0});

auto& ref = x.silu_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0.73105858]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. The self-gated shape, with the small negative region on the left.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0}).silu());

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.1423, -0.2689, 0.0000, 0.7311, 2.8577]

Example 2. The global minimum sits near x = -1.278.

pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({-1.278}).silu());

Output¶

Series(shape=[1], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.2785]

Example 3. The backward is s * (1 + x * (1 - s)) — 0.5 at the origin and briefly negative on the left.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.silu().sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.0881, 0.0723, 0.5000, 0.9277, 1.0881]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • silu() is not monotonic. If you rely on an activation being non-decreasing, this is not it.

  • Floating-point input only; an integer series raises.

  • The forward and the gradient both go slightly negative near x = -1.3.

Summary¶

silu(x) is x * sigmoid(x) — a smooth, self-gating, non-monotonic activation:

  • minimum of about -0.278 near x = -1.278

  • floating-point input only

  • differentiable, backward sigmoid(x) * (1 + x * (1 - sigmoid(x)))

See Also¶

  • Series::gelu: x * Phi(x), the very similar smooth gate.

  • Series::sigmoid: the gate silu() multiplies by.

  • Series::relu: the hard-gate baseline.
